standard.title: Features of familiar places
standard.description: the features of familiar places they belong to, why some places are special and how places can be looked after
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have lived experience of places they inhabit. No formal prior HASS curriculum.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify features of familiar places, explain why some places are special to them, and describe ways places can be looked after.

nodes.label: Features of familiar places
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and describe features of familiar places using observation and simple place vocabulary.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three features of one familiar place (e.g. the school) using provided vocabulary (natural, built, people, activities).
nodes.typical_width: Explore and describe features of multiple familiar places (home, school, neighbourhood, local park); use senses-based observation to identify natural and constructed features.
wider: Compare features of familiar places with places students have visited or seen in stories or on television
Identify features of places in First Nations Australian stories and Dreaming stories, discussing what is special about those places
nodes.hinge_reason: Without feature vocabulary for places, students cannot explain what makes a place special or how to care for it — nodes 2 and 3 both require this observational foundation.

response_modes.reason: Build a working vocabulary of place features through observation walks, photographs and drawings before asking students to describe or evaluate places.

success_criteria: Identifies at least three features of a familiar place
Uses at least two place vocabulary terms (e.g. natural, built, near, far)

nodes.label: Why some places are special
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain why a particular place is special to them or others, connecting significance to personal experience, memory or cultural meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one place that is special to them and give at least one reason why.
nodes.typical_width: Explain why several different places are special to different people; connect significance to ideas such as belonging, memory, basic needs, recreation and cultural or spiritual meaning.
wider: Explore why Country/Place is special and significant to First Nations Australians and how that significance differs from everyday familiarity
Share stories about special places from different cultural backgrounds represented in the class

response_modes.reason: Significance varies by person and culture — using class sharing and diverse stories reveals that 'special' is not one thing.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian concepts of Country/Place offer a qualitatively different type of place significance that enriches all students' understanding of why places matter.
success_criteria: Names at least one place that is special to them
Gives at least one reason why that place is special

nodes.label: How places can be looked after
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can suggest ways to care for a familiar place and describe what would happen if that care was not taken.
nodes.minimum_width: Suggest at least one action to care for a familiar place (e.g. classroom, playground) and explain why that action matters.
nodes.typical_width: Identify multiple ways different places can be cared for; connect care actions to what makes those places important; discuss shared responsibility for looking after places.
wider: Investigate First Nations Australian practices of caring for Country/Place and discuss what these practices involve
Compare how care for a local natural place (e.g. a park or creek) differs from care for a constructed place (e.g. a playground)

response_modes.reason: This node integrates feature knowledge (what is in the place) and significance understanding (why it matters) into action — caring for places because we value them.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one way to care for a familiar place
Connects the care action to the reason the place is valuable
